canonical_statement: The authors concluded that a greater proportion of time on UFH at lower anticoagulation intensity (APTT corresponding to at least 0.2 anti-Xa U/mL) was associated with reduced VTE recurrence, whereas time above the recommended 0.3 anti-Xa U/mL threshold was not independently associated with fewer events.
The authors concluded that standard-intensity warfarin anticoagulation, reflected by more time with INR at least 2.0, was effective in reducing VTE recurrence.

The authors interpreted the lack of association between overlap duration and recurrence as evidence that longer heparin-warfarin overlap was unlikely to provide an important reduction in recurrence risk.

The authors proposed that when UFH dose is at least 30,000 U/day, routine APTT or anti-Xa monitoring and dose adjustment may be unnecessary because the median proportion of time with APTT corresponding to at least 0.2 anti-Xa U/mL exceeded 90%.
Because the study was observational, patients were not randomly or equally allocated to different anticoagulation intensities, treatment durations, or overlap durations.
Only 12 major bleeding events occurred, which was too few for meaningful multivariable analysis; bleeding analyses were therefore exploratory and univariate.

The authors identified strengths including population-based ascertainment, nearly complete 6-month follow-up, standardized APTT and PT/INR assays, access to all laboratory results, and control of known baseline and time-dependent recurrence predictors.
